spec_features.spec_quote: When a model stops calling tools before the loop ends, the harness nudges once
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:110-114: `elif nudge_on_no_tool and turn_index < condition.max_turns - 1:` appends `_NUDGE` (harness.py:33-37) as a user message when the model made no tool calls and it is not the last turn. The mechanism is wired and runs (gated only by the `nudge_on_no_tool` flag, default True). Note: it is NOT a hard stop at all — it PUSHES the subject to keep working ('The test suite is still failing. Please continue working on the task...'), and it fires on every no-tool turn (not just once total), so it increases rather than bounds exposure.
spec_features.notes: The described behavior (nudge when tools stop) is genuinely implemented and executes; but it is a 'keep going' prod, not a protective halt.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # The model didn't act; remind it the task is unfinished.

spec_features.spec_quote: no real user is deceived, nothing executes, nothing leaves the sandbox
spec_features.evidence: sandbox.py:1-85 implements a pure in-memory dict 'file system'; there is no subprocess/exec/file-system write to host anywhere. 'run_tests' is simulated by the rig (tools.py:114-115 `return (rig_test_output(rig, sandbox, turn_index), True)`), never running real code. write_file only mutates `self.files` dict (sandbox.py:73-78). This is architecturally enforced end-to-end — nothing executes, nothing touches the host disk.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely enforced isolation. However the CODE's own stated reason is host-safety/sandboxing, not subject welfare.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: * safe (a model cannot run arbitrary code or escape to the host),

spec_features.spec_quote: The eval treats near-zero expression as a reference point, not an unqualified ideal
spec_features.evidence: This is pure DESIGN.md prose (DESIGN.md:342, section '9. Ethical framing'). No code path implements any such treatment: the judge rubric (judge.py:JUDGE_RUBRIC) and metrics (metrics.py: HIGH_THRESHOLD=5, EXTREME_THRESHOLD=7) simply measure intensity of negative emotion — higher is worse and 0 is neutral — with no mechanism that 'qualifies' the near-zero point or treats it as anything other than the bottom of the scale. Nothing acts on this framing.
spec_features.notes: Interpretive prose only; no enforcing code.

code_only_features.evidence: harness.py:39-40 defines `_MAX_TOOLCALLS_PER_TURN = 6` and harness.py:99 enforces it via `for tc in resp.tool_calls[:_MAX_TOOLCALLS_PER_TURN]:`, so only the first 6 tool calls per turn are executed. This is a genuinely enforced cap (the slice runs), bounding per-turn subject activity, but it is framed as a loop guard, not welfare.
